Name: adaptive_block_size
Title: Adaptive Block Size: Dynamic Context Window Adjustment for Efficient Training
Experiment: Modify the model to dynamically adjust its block size during training, starting with a smaller block size and gradually increasing it. This could potentially lead to faster initial training and better long-range dependency learning.

Name: layerwise_learning_rates
Title: Layer-wise Learning Rate Adaptation: Optimizing Training Dynamics in Transformer Models
Experiment: Implement layer-wise learning rates, where each transformer layer has its own learning rate. Modify the configure_optimizers function to assign different learning rates to different layers, with deeper layers having lower learning rates. Compare the training dynamics, convergence speed, and final performance with the baseline model.

Name: auxiliary_future_heads
Title: Auxiliary Future Prediction Heads for Denser Autoregressive Supervision
Experiment: Add optional horizon-specific auxiliary linear heads to GPT for predicting future characters at offsets 2, 4, and 8 from each hidden state. In GPT.forward, keep the standard lm_head and next-character cross-entropy unchanged, then derive each auxiliary target by shifting the existing targets tensor left by offset-1 positions and filling invalid tail positions with -1 for ignore_index. Train with loss = next_loss + alpha * mean(aux_losses), using alpha=0.25 as the main setting and alpha=0.1 as a small ablation. Generation remains unchanged and uses only the standard lm_head. Update estimate_loss to report comparable next-character train/validation loss separately from the total auxiliary training objective. Compare against baseline using best next-character validation loss, convergence speed, total training time, generated samples, and the small parameter overhead of the auxiliary heads across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8.

Name: warm_ema_self_distillation
Title: Warm-Started EMA Self-Distillation for Character Language Model Generalization
Experiment: Add online self-distillation from an exponential-moving-average teacher model. After initializing GPT, create ema_model as a deepcopy of the uncompiled student, freeze its parameters, and keep it in eval mode. During training, compute the normal next-character cross-entropy loss as usual. After warmup_iters, also run ema_model on the same batch under torch.no_grad() and add a temperature-scaled KL term between student and teacher next-token distributions, averaged over batch and sequence positions: total_loss = ce_loss + alpha_t * temperature^2 * KL(log_softmax(student_logits / temperature), softmax(teacher_logits / temperature)). Ramp alpha_t linearly from 0 to alpha over 1000 iterations after warmup. After each optimizer step, update the teacher with ema_param = ema_decay * ema_param + (1 - ema_decay) * student_param, using the raw uncompiled student parameters if torch.compile is enabled. Keep validation, generation, and final reporting unchanged, using only the standard lm_head and next-character loss. Use one main setting with ema_decay=0.999, temperature=2.0, and alpha=0.15, then compare best validation loss, convergence speed, total train time, inference speed, and generated samples across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8.

Name: suffix_consistency_distillation
Title: Suffix Consistency Distillation for Context-Robust Autoregressive Language Models
Experiment: Add a same-model consistency regularizer between full-context and shortened-context predictions. In the training loop, keep the standard cross-entropy loss on the full 256-token batch X,Y. Also create a fixed shortened view using the final 128 tokens, X_short = X[:, -128:] and Y_short = Y[:, -128:], and run a second forward pass. Align short-context logits with full-context logits from the same suffix positions, detach the full-context logits, and add a temperature-scaled KL loss between the two distributions after ignoring an initial burn-in of 16 positions in the shortened view. Use total_loss = ce_loss + alpha_t * temperature^2 * KL, with alpha_t linearly ramped to alpha during warmup. Test alpha values such as 0.05 and 0.1 with temperature 2.0. Keep validation reporting as ordinary next-character loss on full 256-token contexts for comparability, and additionally evaluate validation loss using shorter context lengths such as 64 and 128 to measure context robustness. Compare best validation loss, convergence speed, training time overhead, inference speed, and generated samples across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8.

Name: gated_causal_conv_mixer
Title: Gated Causal Convolutional Mixing for Local Inductive Bias in Small Autoregressive Transformers
Experiment: Add a lightweight gated causal convolution branch to Transformer blocks. Implement a CausalConvMixer module that applies left-padded depthwise Conv1d over the sequence dimension, GELU, pointwise Linear projection back to n_embd, and dropout. In Block.__init__, add ln_conv, conv_mixer, and a learnable scalar conv_gate initialized to a small value such as 0.05. In Block.forward, insert an additional residual path after attention and before the MLP: x = x + conv_gate * conv_mixer(ln_conv(x)). Keep the standard next-character cross-entropy loss, validation, and generation unchanged. Compare the baseline to two variants: gated convolution in every layer and gated convolution only in the lower half of layers, using kernel size 7 as the main setting. Report best validation loss, convergence speed, total training time, inference tokens per second, and parameter overhead across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8. The hypothesis is that explicit local causal mixing improves sample efficiency and validation loss for character-level language modeling while preserving the Transformer's ability to model longer-range dependencies.

Name: bandpass_token_weighting
Title: Band-Pass Token Difficulty Weighting for Learnable Autoregressive Supervision
Experiment: Modify GPT.forward to optionally return per-token cross-entropy losses by using F.cross_entropy(..., reduction='none') and reshaping the result to batch-by-time. In the training loop, after warmup_iters, compute detached per-token losses and use batch quantiles to identify easy, moderate, and extreme-loss positions. Define weights that downweight losses below the median, upweight losses between the median and 90th percentile, and avoid further upweighting the hardest tail, for example w_easy=0.5, w_mid=1.5, and w_hard=1.0, then normalize weights to mean 1 per batch. Use mean(w * token_loss) as the training objective. Keep estimate_loss, validation, generation, and final reporting based on ordinary unweighted next-character cross-entropy for comparability. Compare against the baseline and a monotonic bounded weighting ablation across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8 using best validation loss, convergence speed, total training time, inference tokens per second, and generated samples.

Name: masked_context_denoising
Title: Masked Context Denoising for Robust Autoregressive Character Models
Experiment: Add stochastic context corruption during training only. Implement corrupt_context(X, vocab_size, corruption_prob) that clones X and randomly replaces selected input tokens with random valid token IDs from the existing vocabulary, returning both the corrupted X and a boolean corruption mask. Modify GPT.forward to optionally return per-token cross-entropy losses using reduction='none', so the training loop can mask out loss terms at positions where the corresponding input token was corrupted while still allowing corrupted earlier prefix tokens to influence later predictions. Ramp corruption_prob from 0 after warmup_iters to values such as 0.02, 0.05, and 0.10. Keep estimate_loss, clean validation, final reporting, and generation unchanged for comparability. Add a robustness evaluation that corrupts validation inputs at fixed rates and reports loss only on positions whose current input token was not corrupted. Compare clean best validation loss, corrupted-context validation loss, convergence speed, total train time, inference tokens per second, and generated samples across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8.

Name: alibi_position_bias
Title: ALiBi Positional Biases for Robust Small Character Transformers
Experiment: Add an optional ALiBi positional-bias mode to the Transformer. Extend GPTConfig with position_encoding choices such as 'absolute', 'alibi', and 'absolute_alibi'. In CausalSelfAttention, add a force_manual_attention flag and use the existing non-flash attention path for all compared variants. For ALiBi variants, construct per-head causal distance biases using standard ALiBi slopes and add them to the attention logits before softmax. In GPT.forward, use learned position embeddings only for 'absolute' and 'absolute_alibi', and omit them for 'alibi'. Keep the standard next-character cross-entropy objective, optimizer, validation, and generation unchanged. Compare absolute embeddings, ALiBi-only, and absolute+ALiBi across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8 under the same attention implementation. Report best validation loss at the normal 256-token context, convergence speed, total train time, inference tokens per second, parameter count, and additional validation losses when batches are cropped to shorter contexts such as 64 and 128 tokens.

Name: tied_confident_exits
Title: Tied Confidence-Based Early Exits for Compute-Adaptive Autoregressive Transformers
Experiment: Modify GPTConfig to add exit_layers and exit_loss_weight. In GPT.__init__, create a small LayerNorm for each selected intermediate exit layer, for example layers 2 and 4 in the 6-layer model, but do not add separate vocabulary heads. In GPT.forward, store hidden states after selected Transformer blocks and compute auxiliary next-character cross-entropy by applying the corresponding exit LayerNorm followed by the existing tied lm_head. Train with total_loss = final_loss + exit_loss_weight * mean(exit_losses), while keeping final_loss separately available for comparable validation. Update estimate_loss to report full-depth train/validation loss and fixed-exit validation losses. Add evaluation modes for fixed exits at layer 2 and layer 4, plus a simple confidence-based generation mode that stops at the earliest exit whose final-token max probability exceeds a threshold, otherwise using the full model. Report validation loss, generated samples, tokens per second, and average layers used for layer-2, layer-4, confidence-exit, and full-depth inference. Compare against the baseline across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8. Main setting: exit_layers=[2,4], exit_loss_weight=0.2, with a small ablation at 0.1.

Name: pooled_prefix_memory
Title: Pooled Prefix Memory Tokens for Efficient Long-Context Autoregressive Modeling
Experiment: Add an optional compressed-prefix memory mechanism to GPT. Modify get_batch to sample prefix_len + block_size + 1 contiguous tokens: prefix_idx contains the first prefix_len tokens, X contains the next block_size tokens, and Y is the usual one-step-shifted target for X. Add a PrefixCompressor module that reuses the token embedding table, divides prefix_idx into memory_slots contiguous chunks, mean-pools each chunk, applies a small projection plus learned slot embeddings, and returns memory token embeddings. Extend GPTConfig with prefix_len, memory_slots, and prefix_dropout. Increase the model's positional capacity to block_size + memory_slots when memory is enabled. In GPT.forward, prepend compressed memory embeddings before normal token embeddings and compute cross-entropy only on the suffix token positions. With probability prefix_dropout during training, replace compressed prefix memory with learned null memory tokens so the model remains usable when no prefix is available. Keep generation unchanged except that forward passes use null memory unless prefix_idx is explicitly provided. Compare the baseline 256-token GPT against memory models with prefix_len=256 and memory_slots in {8, 16, 32}. Report best validation loss with prefix enabled, validation loss with null memory, convergence speed, training-time overhead, inference tokens per second, parameter overhead, and generated samples across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8.

Name: position_shift_augmentation
Title: Position Shift Augmentation for Translation-Robust Character Transformers
Experiment: Extend GPTConfig with max_position_offset and allocate the learned position embedding table with size block_size + max_position_offset while keeping the causal context length block_size unchanged. In GPT.forward, during training sample a random integer offset in [0, max_position_offset] and use positions offset:offset+t; during validation and generation use offset 0 for clean comparability. Add an optional forward argument position_offset so estimate_loss can run validation probes at fixed offsets such as 0, 16, 32, and 64. Compare the baseline against variants with max_position_offset values such as 32 and 64. Report best clean validation loss, shifted-position validation losses, convergence speed, total training time, inference tokens per second, parameter overhead, and generated samples across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8.

Name: self_recovery_training
Title: Self-Recovery Training for Exposure-Bias-Robust Character Language Models
Experiment: Add a training-only self-recovery auxiliary objective. In the training loop, compute the standard clean forward pass on X,Y and keep its cross-entropy as the primary loss. After warmup_iters, use the clean logits under torch.no_grad() to produce one-step model predictions for each position, using multinomial sampling at temperature 1.0 as the main setting and argmax as an ablation. Construct X_self by copying X and replacing a small ramped fraction of X[:, 1:] with predictions from logits[:, :-1], so the model conditions on its own plausible previous-token mistakes while targets Y remain unchanged. Run a second forward pass on X_self,Y and train with total_loss = clean_loss + alpha_t * self_loss, where alpha_t ramps from 0 to alpha over 1000 iterations after warmup. Test alpha values such as 0.1 and 0.25 with max replacement probabilities 0.05 and 0.10. Keep normal estimate_loss, clean validation, generation, and final reporting unchanged for comparability. Add a self-conditioned validation probe that applies the same replacement procedure without gradients and reports recovery loss. Compare best clean validation loss, self-conditioned validation loss, convergence speed, total train time, inference tokens per second, and generated samples across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8.

Name: domain_conditioned_multicorpus_lm
Title: Domain-Conditioned Multi-Corpus Character Language Modeling
Experiment: Add a multi_dataset training mode that jointly trains on shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8. Build a global character vocabulary from the union of each dataset's meta.pkl vocabulary, and create per-dataset local-id to global-id remapping tensors used inside get_batch. Extend GPTConfig with n_domains and use_domain_embedding. In GPT.__init__, add a learned domain embedding table with one vector per dataset when enabled. In GPT.forward, accept domain_id and add the corresponding domain embedding to token embeddings before dropout. Train one shared model by sampling one dataset uniformly each iteration, remapping its batch to the global vocabulary, and passing the dataset domain_id. Evaluate validation loss separately for each dataset using its domain_id. Compare three settings: the original separate per-dataset models, a shared model without domain embeddings, and a shared model with domain embeddings. Report per-dataset best validation loss, macro-average validation loss, convergence speed, total training time, inference tokens per second, generated samples conditioned on each domain, and total parameter count relative to training three separate models.

Name: multiscale_attention_horizons
Title: Multiscale Attention Horizons for Context-Robust Autoregressive Transformers
Experiment: Add optional horizon-limited causal attention to CausalSelfAttention. Extend GPTConfig with attention_horizon_choices and attention_horizon_training. In GPT.forward, when training and horizon training is enabled, sample one horizon per forward pass from choices such as [64, 128, 256], then pass it through Block.forward into CausalSelfAttention.forward. The attention mask should remain causal but additionally prevent each token from attending to keys more than horizon positions in the past. Use horizon 256 as the full-context case, so the model still frequently trains with the original context length. Keep the standard next-character cross-entropy objective, optimizer, generation, and clean validation unchanged. Add validation probes that run with fixed horizons 64, 128, and 256 to measure context robustness. Compare against the baseline using best full-context validation loss, short-horizon validation loss, convergence speed, total training time, inference tokens per second, and generated samples across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8. Main setting: attention_horizon_choices=[64,128,256], with an ablation [32,64,128,256].

Name: recurrent_depth_sharing
Title: Recurrent Depth Sharing for Parameter-Efficient Character Transformers
Experiment: Extend GPTConfig with depth_sharing choices 'none', 'full', and 'cyclic', plus num_shared_blocks and use_depth_embeddings. In GPT.__init__, keep the current independent ModuleList for 'none'. For 'full', create one Block and reuse it for all n_layer applications. For 'cyclic', create num_shared_blocks Blocks and reuse them cyclically across the n_layer depth steps, for example two shared blocks over six applications. If use_depth_embeddings is enabled, add a learned depth embedding to the hidden state before each block application so shared blocks can condition on the recurrence step. Keep the standard next-character cross-entropy objective, optimizer, validation, and generation unchanged. Compare the untied 6-layer baseline against full sharing and 2-block cyclic sharing, with and without depth embeddings as a small ablation. Report best validation loss, convergence speed, total train time, inference tokens per second, generated samples, parameter count, and validation loss per million parameters across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8. The hypothesis is that recurrent depth sharing improves parameter efficiency and regularization while preserving much of the benefit of Transformer depth.

Name: detached_prefix_memory
Title: Detached Prefix Memory for Long-Context Character Language Modeling
Experiment: Add an optional detached hidden-state memory mechanism. Extend GPTConfig with use_prefix_memory and memory_len. Modify get_batch to optionally sample prefix_len + block_size + 1 contiguous tokens, returning prefix_idx, X, and Y, where X and Y remain the ordinary suffix training block. Modify GPT.forward to support two modes: a memory-building no-gradient prefix pass that returns the last memory_len hidden states from each Transformer layer, and a normal suffix pass that accepts these per-layer memories. Modify CausalSelfAttention.forward to concatenate each layer's memory states to current keys and values, while queries are only current suffix tokens and the causal mask allows attending to all memory positions plus previous suffix positions. Train with the standard next-character cross-entropy only on suffix tokens. Compare baseline training against prefix-memory variants with memory_len values such as 64, 128, and 256. Report clean validation loss with memory enabled and disabled, convergence speed, total train time, inference tokens per second, generated samples, and parameter overhead across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8.

Name: discounted_future_distribution
Title: Distance-Discounted Future Distribution Prediction for Autoregressive Representation Learning
Experiment: Add a lightweight auxiliary objective that asks each hidden state to predict a distance-weighted distribution of characters appearing in its near future. In GPT.__init__, add an optional future_window_head = nn.Linear(n_embd, vocab_size, bias=False). In GPT.forward, keep the standard tied lm_head and next-character cross-entropy unchanged, but when targets are provided and the auxiliary option is enabled, also compute aux_logits = future_window_head(x). For each position, build a soft target distribution from targets[:, t:t+W] using weights gamma^k for future offsets k, normalizing over valid positions; use W=16 and gamma=0.9 as the main setting. Compute auxiliary loss as soft cross-entropy between log_softmax(aux_logits) and this discounted future distribution. Train with total_loss = next_loss + alpha * future_distribution_loss, using alpha=0.1 as the main setting and small ablations alpha=0.05, W in {8, 32}, plus a flat unweighted-window variant. Keep estimate_loss, validation, final reporting, and generation based on the ordinary next-character lm_head for comparability. Compare against the baseline across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8 using best validation loss, convergence speed, total training time, inference tokens per second, generated samples, and auxiliary-head parameter overhead.

Name: next_span_contrastive
Title: Next-Span Contrastive Prediction for Chunk-Aware Autoregressive Modeling
Experiment: Add a lightweight contrastive auxiliary objective that trains hidden states to identify their true upcoming character span among in-batch negatives. Extend GPTConfig with use_span_contrastive, span_len, num_span_anchors, span_loss_weight, and span_temperature. In GPT.__init__, add an anchor projection, a span projection, and learned relative span position embeddings. In GPT.forward, keep the standard next-character lm_head and cross-entropy unchanged, but add optional arguments span_loss_weight_current and return_aux_info. When targets are provided, the model is in training mode, use_span_contrastive is enabled, and span_loss_weight_current > 0, randomly sample num_span_anchors valid anchor positions where a future span of length span_len is available. For each anchor, encode targets[:, anchor:anchor+span_len] using the tied token embedding table plus relative span embeddings, mean-pool the span representation, and project it. Project the hidden state x[:, anchor, :], L2-normalize both projected vectors, compute batch-by-batch similarities divided by span_temperature, and apply InfoNCE cross-entropy with diagonal positives. The returned training loss is next_token_loss + span_loss_weight_current * mean(span_losses). In the training loop, ramp span_loss_weight_current linearly from 0 to span_loss_weight after warmup_iters. Because the auxiliary loss is disabled in eval mode and generation, estimate_loss, validation, final reporting, and sampling remain based on ordinary next-character loss. Add a small diagnostic that reports next-span retrieval accuracy on validation batches. Compare the baseline to span contrastive training with span_len=16, num_span_anchors=2, span_loss_weight=0.05, span_temperature=0.1, plus one ablation at span_loss_weight=0.1 across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8. Report best validation loss, convergence speed, total training time, inference tokens per second, generated samples, retrieval accuracy, and auxiliary parameter overhead.

Name: confidence_ngram_distillation
Title: Confidence-Gated N-Gram Distillation for Sample-Efficient Character Transformers
Experiment: Build a fixed smoothed backoff n-gram teacher from each dataset's train.bin before training, using orders up to 5 and no validation data. Store next-character count dictionaries for each context order and compute a teacher confidence from the selected context count. During training, keep the standard next-character cross-entropy unchanged. After warmup_iters, sample a small subset of token positions from each batch, query the highest-order available teacher distribution for each context, keep and renormalize the top-k teacher probabilities, and add a KL distillation loss between the student's restricted top-k distribution and the teacher's top-k distribution. Weight each sampled position by a confidence factor such as count / (count + c), and ramp the global distillation weight alpha_t from 0 to alpha over 1000 iterations. Validation, generation, and final reporting remain based on ordinary next-character cross-entropy with no n-gram teacher at inference. Compare the baseline against max_order=3 and max_order=5 teachers with top_k=16 and alpha values 0.05 and 0.1 across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8. Report best validation loss, early convergence speed, train-time overhead, inference tokens per second, generated samples, teacher coverage, teacher-only validation loss, and student-teacher agreement over training.

Name: stochastic_time_reversal
Title: Stochastic Time-Reversal Training for Regularized Causal Language Models
Experiment: Add an optional stochastic_time_reversal training mode. Extend GPTConfig with use_direction_embedding and n_directions=2. In GPT.__init__, add a learned direction embedding table when enabled. In GPT.forward, accept an optional direction_id argument, either an integer or a per-example tensor, and add the corresponding direction embedding to token embeddings before dropout. In the training loop, keep get_batch unchanged. For each batch, construct reverse examples from the same contiguous windows with X_rev = torch.flip(Y, dims=[1]) and Y_rev = torch.flip(X, dims=[1]). After warmup_iters, ramp a reverse probability p_t from 0 to p over 1000 iterations. Sample a boolean mask over batch examples; masked examples use X_rev,Y_rev,direction_id=1, and unmasked examples use X,Y,direction_id=0. Train with the ordinary cross-entropy loss on this mixed batch, requiring only one forward/backward pass per iteration. Use p=0.25 as the main setting, with ablations p=0.5 and no direction embedding. Keep validation, generation, final reporting, and inference speed measurement forward-only with direction_id=0 for direct comparability to the baseline. Add a diagnostic reverse validation loss using fully reversed validation batches. Compare across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8 using best forward validation loss, convergence speed, total training time, inference tokens per second, generated samples, reverse validation loss, and parameter overhead.

Name: causal_pause_tokens
Title: Causal Pause Tokens for Internal Deliberation in Autoregressive Language Models
Experiment: Extend GPTConfig with pause_steps and use_pause_step_embeddings. Keep block_size as the number of real dataset tokens, but allocate the position embedding table and any non-flash causal attention mask for an internal length of block_size * (pause_steps + 1). In GPT.__init__, add a learned pause token embedding and optional learned pause step embeddings. Modify GPT.forward so that when pause_steps > 0 it embeds the normal input tokens, inserts pause_steps learned pause embeddings after every real token, runs the existing causal Transformer over the expanded internal sequence, and computes next-character logits only from the final pause position after each real token. Targets remain the original Y tensor, so loss is ordinary next-character cross-entropy over real character positions only. For targets=None generation, return logits from the final pause position after the last real token, ensuring generated samples contain only dataset characters. Keep get_batch, validation splits, optimizer, and sampling protocol unchanged. Compare the baseline to pause_steps=1 as the main setting, with smaller ablations using pause_steps=2, disabling pause step embeddings, and a compute-aware pause_steps=1 run with a shorter real block_size so the internal sequence length matches the baseline. Report best validation loss, convergence speed, total training time, emitted-character inference tokens per second, generated samples, and parameter/compute overhead across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8.

Name: loss_aware_span_replay
Title: Loss-Aware Span Replay for Sample-Efficient Autoregressive Language Modeling
Experiment: Add a fixed-size online replay buffer that stores training span start indices and an EMA of their detached per-example cross-entropy loss. Modify get_batch to optionally return sampled start indices and to accept a list of replay start indices for part of the batch. Modify GPT.forward or the training loop to obtain per-example losses using reduction='none' reshaped to batch by time, while keeping the ordinary mean next-character loss as the optimization objective. During warmup_iters, train exactly as the baseline and populate the buffer from uniformly sampled spans. After warmup, construct each training batch from a mixture of uniform spans and replay spans, using replay_fraction values such as 0.25 and 0.5. Sample replay spans from a clipped high-loss band, for example excluding the lowest 50 percent and highest 5 percent of buffered EMA losses, to focus on informative but not extreme spans. Keep estimate_loss, validation, generation, and final reporting based on uniform next-character loss for comparability. Compare against the baseline across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8, reporting best validation loss, convergence speed, total train time, inference tokens per second, generated samples, replay-buffer coverage, replay diversity, mean replay loss, and sampling overhead.

Name: latent_state_transition
Title: Latent State Transition Prediction for Autoregressive Representation Learning
Experiment: Extend GPTConfig with use_latent_transition and transition_loss_weight. In GPT.__init__, add a lightweight transition_mlp that takes concat(hidden_t, embedding(next_token)) and predicts a residual update in hidden space. In GPT.forward, keep the standard lm_head and next-character cross-entropy unchanged. When targets are provided, the model is training, use_latent_transition is enabled, and the current auxiliary weight is positive, use final hidden states x after ln_f. For positions 0 through T-2, form inputs from x[:, :-1, :] and detached tied token embeddings of targets[:, :-1], predict next_state_pred = x[:, :-1, :] + transition_mlp(...), and compute a cosine-distance loss against x[:, 1:, :].detach() after normalizing both tensors. Train with total_loss = next_token_loss + alpha_t * transition_loss, where alpha_t ramps from 0 to transition_loss_weight after warmup_iters. Keep estimate_loss, validation, final reporting, and generation based on ordinary next-character loss for comparability. Add an optional diagnostic reporting validation latent transition cosine error. Compare the baseline against transition_loss_weight values such as 0.05, 0.1, and 0.2 across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8, measuring best validation loss, convergence speed, total training time, inference tokens per second, generated samples, and auxiliary parameter overhead.

Name: entropy_adaptive_smoothing
Title: Entropy-Adaptive Contextual Smoothing for Ambiguous Next-Token Supervision
Experiment: Precompute short-context continuation statistics from each dataset's train.bin using context orders 1 to 3 and no validation data. For each observed context, store its count, top-k next-character probabilities, and entropy normalized by log(vocab_size). Keep the GPT architecture unchanged. In the training loop, compute logits and the ordinary one-hot next-character cross-entropy as usual. After warmup_iters, look up the highest-order available context for each batch position, falling back to shorter contexts or no smoothing when counts are too small. Compute a sparse contextual soft cross-entropy against the stored top-k continuation distribution, and blend it with the one-hot loss using epsilon_pos = epsilon_max * ramp * normalized_entropy, so low-entropy contexts remain nearly one-hot while ambiguous contexts receive more smoothing. Test epsilon_max values such as 0.05, 0.1, and 0.2 with top_k=16. Keep estimate_loss, validation, generation, final reporting, and inference speed based on ordinary one-hot next-character loss for direct comparability. Compare against the baseline, uniform label smoothing, and fixed contextual smoothing across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8 using best validation loss, convergence speed, total training time, inference tokens per second, generated samples, and simple calibration diagnostics such as average validation confidence.

Name: causal_cache_contrast
Title: Causal Cache-Contrastive Regularization for Retrieval-Compatible Autoregressive Representations
Experiment: Modify GPT.forward to optionally return final hidden states before the lm_head in addition to logits and ordinary next-character loss. Add a causal_cache_contrast_loss function that normalizes hidden states and, for each position t, compares h_t to detached hidden states from earlier positions within a fixed cache_window. Use the next-token targets of earlier positions as cache labels. For positions whose true target appears at least once in the causal cache, maximize the softmax similarity mass assigned to earlier positions with the same target, using a temperature-scaled supervised contrastive loss. Compute this auxiliary loss only after warmup_iters and optionally on a random subset of valid positions to limit overhead. Train with total_loss = next_token_loss + alpha_t * cache_contrast_loss, where alpha_t ramps linearly to cache_loss_weight. Keep standard validation, generation, and final reporting based on the normal lm_head for comparability. Add a cache-augmented validation diagnostic that interpolates model probabilities with a causal neural-cache distribution built from hidden-state similarities. Compare the baseline against cache_window values 64 and 128, cache_loss_weight values 0.05 and 0.1, and cache interpolation weights 0.1 and 0.2 across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8. Report best ordinary validation loss, cache-augmented validation loss, convergence speed, total training time, inference tokens per second without cache, generated samples, valid cache-match rate, and average cache confidence.

Name: suffix_repetition_unlikelihood
Title: Suffix-Conditioned Repetition Unlikelihood for Degeneration-Resistant Character Language Models
Experiment: Keep the GPT architecture, generation code, and ordinary next-character cross-entropy unchanged. Add a suffix_repetition_unlikelihood_loss(logits, X, targets, suffix_lengths, window, max_positions) helper used only during training. For a random subset of token positions, look at suffixes of the current prefix with lengths 2 and 3. Within a recent context window, find previous occurrences of the same suffix and collect the tokens that followed those occurrences. Keep estimate_loss, validation, generation, and final reporting based on ordinary next-character cross-entropy for comparability. Report best validation loss, convergence speed, total train time, inference tokens per second, generated samples, validation calibration, average predictive velocity, and repeated n-gram diagnostics across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8.

Name: causal_history_sketching
Title: Causal History Sketch Prediction for Multi-Scale Autoregressive State Learning
Experiment: Add a training-only auxiliary objective that asks each final hidden state to predict multi-scale summaries of the strictly previous context. Extend GPTConfig with use_history_sketching, history_sketch_windows, history_sketch_min_tokens, history_sketch_loss_weight, and history_sketch_ramp_iters. In GPT.__init__, add one lightweight Linear(n_embd, vocab_size) sketch head per history window. Modify GPT.forward to optionally return final hidden states and, when targets are provided, compute the ordinary next-character cross-entropy exactly as before. During training after warmup, build soft sketch targets from idx only: for each position t and window W, compute the normalized character histogram over idx[:, max(0, t-W):t], excluding the current token and ignoring positions with fewer than history_sketch_min_tokens previous characters. These targets can be computed with one-hot encodings and cumulative sums over the sequence dimension. Compute soft cross-entropy between each sketch head's logits and its corresponding history histogram, then optimize total_loss = next_token_loss + alpha_t * mean(history_sketch_losses), where alpha_t ramps from 0 to history_sketch_loss_weight after warmup_iters. Keep estimate_loss, best validation loss, final reporting, generation, and inference speed based on the ordinary next-character lm_head for comparability. Add separate diagnostics for sketch validation cross-entropy, top-k sketch mass assigned to actually observed recent characters, cropped-context validation losses at 64 and 128 tokens, and parameter overhead. Compare the baseline against history_sketch_windows=[16, 64, 256] with history_sketch_loss_weight values 0.02 and 0.05, plus a single-window ablation using only window 64, across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8.

Name: causal_recurrence_embeddings
Title: Causal Recurrence Embeddings for Copy-Aware Autoregressive Language Modeling
Experiment: Extend GPTConfig with use_recurrence_embeddings, recurrence_num_buckets, recurrence_max_distance, use_recurrence_auxiliary, recurrence_aux_weight, and recurrence_aux_ramp_iters. Add a helper that computes logarithmic previous-occurrence distance buckets from idx only: for each position, use one reserved bucket when the current token has not appeared earlier in the same sequence, otherwise bucket the distance to its most recent previous occurrence up to recurrence_max_distance. In GPT.__init__, add a learned recurrence bucket embedding table and a scalar gate initialized near zero, and in GPT.forward add the gated recurrence embedding to tok_emb before position embeddings and dropout. For the auxiliary variant, add two small heads from the final hidden state: one predicts whether the next target token appears anywhere in the visible prefix, and one predicts the previous-occurrence distance bucket for that next token, using ignore_index for positions where no previous occurrence exists. Train with total_loss = next_token_loss + alpha_t * auxiliary_loss, ramping alpha_t after warmup_iters with recurrence_aux_weight values such as 0.05 and 0.1. Keep estimate_loss, validation, final reporting, and sampling based on ordinary next-character loss, with generation recomputing recurrence buckets from the generated prefix. Compare the baseline against recurrence embeddings alone and recurrence embeddings plus the auxiliary loss across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8. Report best validation loss, convergence speed, total training time, inference tokens per second, generated samples, parameter overhead, next-token recurrence accuracy, distance-bucket accuracy, target-in-prefix rate, and repeated n-gram diagnostics.

Name: future_ngram_sketching
Title: Hashed Future N-Gram Sketch Prediction for Tokenization-Free Language Models
Experiment: Add a training-only auxiliary objective that asks each hidden state to predict a compact hashed sketch of short n-grams appearing in its near future. Extend GPTConfig with use_future_ngram_sketching, sketch_ngram_orders, sketch_window, sketch_num_buckets, sketch_loss_weight, and sketch_ramp_iters. In GPT.__init__, add one Linear(n_embd, sketch_num_buckets) sketch head per selected n-gram order, using orders [2, 3], sketch_window=16, and sketch_num_buckets=512 as the main setting. Modify GPT.forward to optionally return final hidden states before the lm_head while preserving the standard logits and next-character cross-entropy behavior. Add a future_ngram_sketch_loss helper that builds multi-hot bucket targets from targets: for each position, hash every valid future n-gram of the chosen order starting within the next sketch_window characters into a bucket, then compute a balanced BCEWithLogits loss that upweights positive buckets and ignores tail positions with no valid future n-grams. In the training loop, after warmup_iters, ramp alpha_t to sketch_loss_weight and optimize total_loss = next_token_loss + alpha_t * mean(sketch_losses). Keep estimate_loss, clean validation, final reporting, generation, and inference speed based on ordinary next-character loss for comparability. Add diagnostics for sketch validation BCE, top-k bucket recall, clean best validation loss, convergence speed, total training time, generated samples, and auxiliary parameter overhead. Compare the baseline against sketch_window values 16 and 32, sketch_num_buckets values 512 and 1024, and sketch_loss_weight values 0.02 and 0.05 across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8.

Name: representation_entropy_calibration
Title: Representation-Based Entropy Calibration for Ambiguous Autoregressive Contexts
Experiment: Modify GPT.forward to optionally return final hidden states before the lm_head, while preserving the standard logits and next-character cross-entropy behavior. Add a training-only representation_entropy_calibration_loss helper. After warmup_iters, sample a modest number of anchor positions from the batch, for example 256 batch-time positions, and build a detached candidate pool of hidden states from other batch examples, optionally also allowing earlier positions from the same sequence but never later positions. L2-normalize detached hidden states, find the top-k nearest candidate prefix representations for each anchor, and form an empirical neighbor continuation histogram from the corresponding next-character targets. Compute the normalized entropy of this neighbor histogram as an ambiguity target, weighting anchors by mean neighbor similarity and requiring at least two valid neighbor labels. Compute the model's normalized predictive entropy from its logits at the same anchor positions, and add a squared-error penalty between model entropy and detached neighbor entropy. Train with total_loss = ce_loss + alpha_t * entropy_calibration_loss, ramping alpha_t from 0 to alpha after warmup_iters. Keep estimate_loss, validation, generation, final reporting, and inference speed based on ordinary next-character cross-entropy with no nearest-neighbor computation. Add diagnostics for validation confidence calibration, average predictive entropy, negative log likelihood by confidence bucket, and agreement between model entropy and neighbor entropy. Compare the baseline against alpha values 0.01, 0.03, and 0.1 with top-k values 8 and 16 across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8.

Name: contextual_fast_adapters
Title: Contextual Fast Adapters for Test-Time Self-Supervised Language Model Adaptation
Experiment: Add optional low-rank residual adapters to each Transformer block: apply a small LayerNorm, down-project from n_embd to rank r, apply GELU, up-project back to n_embd, zero-initialize the up projection, and add the result as a residual branch after the MLP. Train the model with the standard next-character cross-entropy, unchanged generation, and unchanged ordinary validation; include one simple ablation where only adapter parameters are trained for the first few hundred iterations before unfreezing the full model. Add a prefix-adaptation validation routine that samples contiguous validation blocks, splits each block into an observed prefix and held-out suffix, saves the adapter parameters, freezes all non-adapter weights, takes 1 to 3 SGD steps on prefix next-token loss, re-runs the full block, reports cross-entropy only on suffix positions, and then restores the saved adapter parameters. Compare ordinary validation loss, no-adaptation suffix loss, prefix-adapted suffix loss, adaptation on mismatched prefixes as a negative control, adaptation overhead, adapter parameter count, and generated samples after adapting on a prompt prefix. Run ablations over adapter rank, prefix length, adaptation learning rate, number of adaptation steps, and adapters-only versus adapters-plus-LayerNorm adaptation across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8.

Name: scale_conditioned_strided_lm
Title: Scale-Conditioned Strided Language Modeling for Multi-Timescale Character Transformers
Experiment: Add an auxiliary multi-resolution language modeling objective using strided subsequences. Modify get_batch to accept a stride argument s. For stride s, sample a raw span long enough to form x_t = data[i + t*s] and y_t = data[i + (t+1)*s] for t in 0..block_size-1, so the model predicts the next character in a downsampled sequence covering a larger raw context. Extend GPTConfig with use_stride_embedding and stride_values, add a small learned stride embedding table in GPT.__init__, initialize it to zero, and modify GPT.forward to accept stride_id and add the corresponding embedding to token embeddings before position embeddings. During training, always compute ordinary contiguous stride-1 cross-entropy as the main loss. After warmup_iters, sample one auxiliary stride from {2, 4}, compute a second forward pass on that strided batch, and optimize total_loss = loss_stride1 + alpha_t * loss_strided, ramping alpha_t over 1000 iterations to values such as 0.1 or 0.25. Keep estimate_loss, best validation loss, final reporting, generation, and inference speed based on ordinary stride-1 inputs with stride_id=0 for direct comparability. Add validation probes for stride-2 and stride-4 downsampled losses, plus a small ablation without stride embeddings to test whether explicit scale conditioning matters. Compare against the baseline across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8, reporting clean best validation loss, strided validation losses, convergence speed, total train time, inference tokens per second, generated samples, and stride-embedding parameter overhead.

Name: adversarial_position_scrubbing
Title: Adversarial Position Scrubbing for Translation-Robust Autoregressive Transformers
Experiment: Add a lightweight training-only adversarial classifier that discourages final hidden states from making absolute block position linearly decodable. Implement a GradReverse autograd function and extend GPTConfig with use_position_adversary, position_adv_weight, position_adv_ramp_iters, and position_adv_sample_positions. In GPT.__init__, add pos_adv_head = nn.Linear(n_embd, block_size). Modify GPT.forward to optionally return final hidden states after ln_f. In the training loop, keep the ordinary next-character cross-entropy as the primary loss. After warmup_iters, randomly sample up to position_adv_sample_positions batch-time hidden states, pass them through gradient reversal with a ramped coefficient, predict their absolute timestep with pos_adv_head, and add the resulting position classification loss to the training objective. The classifier learns to predict position, while the Transformer trunk receives reversed gradients scaled by the ramped adversarial weight. Keep estimate_loss, clean validation, final reporting, inference speed, and generation based only on the standard lm_head. Add diagnostics for adversarial position accuracy, a detached validation position-probe accuracy, cropped-context validation losses at 64 and 128 tokens, and shifted-position validation losses using an optional position_offset argument in GPT.forward. Compare the baseline against position_adv_weight values such as 0.01, 0.03, and 0.1 across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8, reporting best clean validation loss, robustness to shifted and cropped contexts, convergence speed, total train time, inference tokens per second, generated samples, and whether reduced position decodability correlates with better context robustness.

Name: confidence_knn_distillation
Title: Confidence-Weighted kNN Distillation from Recent Hidden-State Memories
Experiment: Modify GPT.forward to optionally return final hidden states before the lm_head while preserving the standard logits and next-character cross-entropy behavior. Add a RecentKNNCache helper that stores a FIFO queue of detached, L2-normalized float16 hidden states and their next-character targets from recent training batches only. During training, after warmup_iters and every knn_interval iterations, sample up to knn_num_anchors batch-time positions from the current forward pass, query the cache by cosine similarity, retrieve top-k neighbors, and build a sparse soft next-token target by softmaxing neighbor similarities with temperature knn_temperature and scatter-adding weights by neighbor target token. Compute a confidence score for each anchor from the cache target distribution, such as 1 minus normalized entropy or the maximum token probability, and use it to weight the auxiliary soft cross-entropy from the student's logits to the cache-derived target. Train with total_loss = next_token_loss + alpha_t * mean(confidence * knn_loss), ramping alpha_t from 0 to alpha over knn_ramp_iters. Update the cache after each optimizer step using detached hidden states and targets from the current batch. Keep estimate_loss, clean validation, generation, final reporting, and inference speed based on the ordinary lm_head with no cache required. Add diagnostics for neighbor target agreement, cache-target entropy, average top-k similarity, kNN-only validation loss using a train-built cache, and training overhead. Use a main setting such as cache_size=32768, top_k=16, knn_num_anchors=512, knn_interval=4, knn_temperature=0.07, and alpha=0.05, with small ablations over alpha, top_k, and confidence weighting across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8.

Name: batchwise_latent_cpc
Title: Batchwise Multi-Horizon Latent Predictive Coding for Autoregressive Transformers
Experiment: Modify GPT.forward to optionally return final hidden states after ln_f in addition to logits and the ordinary next-character cross-entropy. Extend GPTConfig with use_latent_cpc, cpc_horizons, cpc_proj_dim, cpc_loss_weight, cpc_temperature, cpc_anchors_per_horizon, and cpc_ramp_iters. In GPT.__init__, add one linear predictor per horizon and one shared linear projection to the CPC dimension. During training, keep standard next-token cross-entropy as the primary loss. After warmup_iters, for each horizon h in cpc_horizons such as [4, 16, 64], sample a small set of anchor positions t that are valid for all batch examples. For each anchor, project hidden[:, t] through the horizon predictor, project hidden[:, t+h].detach() through the shared projection, L2-normalize both, and compute a B-by-B InfoNCE loss where each example's own future state is the positive and other batch examples are negatives. Ramp the auxiliary weight to cpc_loss_weight over cpc_ramp_iters and train with total_loss = next_token_loss + alpha_t * mean(cpc_losses). Keep estimate_loss, validation loss, generation, final reporting, and inference speed based only on the ordinary lm_head. Add validation diagnostics for horizon retrieval accuracy, positive similarity, negative similarity, and train-time overhead, computed with no auxiliary gradients. Compare the baseline against cpc_horizons=[4,16,64] with cpc_loss_weight values 0.03 and 0.1, plus a local-only ablation [4,16], across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8.

Name: self_contrastive_rollout_ranking
Title: Self-Contrastive Rollout Ranking for Sequence-Level Autoregressive Training
Experiment: Keep the GPT architecture, standard next-character cross-entropy, validation, and generation code unchanged. Add a helper score_continuations(model, prefix, continuations) that concatenates each prefix with a candidate continuation, runs one forward pass on combined[:, :-1], computes log_softmax logits, gathers log probabilities for combined[:, 1:], and averages only the continuation target positions starting at prefix_len - 1. In the training loop, after warmup_iters and only every rank_interval iterations, take a small sub-batch from X, use the first prefix_len tokens as the prefix and the following rollout_len tokens as the real continuation. Temporarily switch the model to eval mode and sample a generated continuation of length rollout_len from the same prefix under torch.no_grad(), then restore train mode. Score the real and generated continuations together with gradient tracking, skip exact-match negatives, and add rank_loss = softplus(margin - (score_real - score_generated) / rank_temperature). Train with total_loss = ce_loss + alpha_t * rank_loss, ramping alpha_t from 0 to alpha after warmup. Use prefix_len=128, rollout_len=16 or 32, rank_batch_size=8, rank_interval=10 or 20, alpha values 0.03 and 0.05, margin=0, and rank_temperature=1.0 as main settings. Keep estimate_loss, best validation loss, final reporting, and inference speed based on ordinary next-character loss for comparability. Add diagnostics for ranking accuracy, real-vs-generated score gap, repeated 3-gram and 5-gram rates in generated samples, generated entropy, exact-match negative rate, and training-time overhead across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8.

Name: subsampled_causal_vat
Title: Subsampled Causal Virtual Adversarial Training for Robust Character Language Models
Experiment: Modify GPT.forward to optionally accept input_embeds_override and optionally return token embeddings before position embeddings. In the training loop, keep the standard full-batch clean forward pass on X,Y and optimize ordinary next-character cross-entropy as the primary loss. After warmup_iters, and only every vat_interval iterations, take a small sub-batch from the current batch and use its detached clean logits as teacher predictions. Compute detached token embeddings for this sub-batch, add a small normalized random perturbation, and run one probe forward pass through the model using input_embeds_override. Compute KL divergence from the detached clean distribution to the probe distribution, then use torch.autograd.grad only with respect to the perturbation to obtain a virtual adversarial direction. Detach and normalize this direction, recompute non-detached token embeddings for the same sub-batch, run a final adversarial forward pass with embeddings plus vat_epsilon times the direction, and add a ramped KL consistency loss to the clean objective. Keep estimate_loss, best validation loss, generation, final reporting, and inference speed based on the ordinary clean model. Add diagnostics for validation loss under random embedding noise, validation loss under one-step adversarial embedding perturbations, predictive KL sharpness, confidence calibration, and train-time overhead. Compare the baseline against vat_epsilon values 0.5 and 1.0 times embedding RMS, alpha values 0.03 and 0.1, and vat_interval values 2 and 4 across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8.

Name: bootstrap_output_ensembles
Title: Bootstrap Output Ensembles for Calibrated Autoregressive Character Modeling
Experiment: Add an optional lightweight bootstrapped output ensemble on top of the shared GPT trunk. Extend GPTConfig with use_bootstrap_heads, num_bootstrap_heads, bootstrap_rank, bootstrap_keep_prob, bootstrap_loss_weight, and ensemble_eval. In GPT.__init__, keep the existing tied lm_head unchanged and add num_bootstrap_heads low-rank residual output heads, each implemented as Linear(n_embd, bootstrap_rank), GELU, and Linear(bootstrap_rank, vocab_size), with the final projection zero-initialized so training starts at the baseline. In GPT.forward, compute base_logits normally, then compute member logits as base_logits plus each residual head when enabled. During training with targets, compute the ordinary base next-character cross-entropy and also per-token cross-entropies for each bootstrap member. For each member, sample an independent Bernoulli mask over batch-time positions with probability bootstrap_keep_prob, normalize by the number of kept positions, and optimize total_loss = base_loss + bootstrap_loss_weight * mean(masked_member_losses), using bootstrap_loss_weight=0.5 as the main setting. During validation and generation, support base-only logits and ensemble logits formed by averaging probabilities from the base head and all bootstrap members, returning log probabilities for compatibility with the existing sampling code. Report base validation loss, ensemble validation loss, best validation loss for both modes, confidence-binned calibration error, average member disagreement, total training time, inference tokens per second for base and ensemble decoding, parameter overhead, and generated samples. Compare the baseline against num_bootstrap_heads values 2 and 4 with bootstrap_rank values 32 and 64 across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8.

Name: self_induced_segment_targets
Title: Self-Induced Segment Targets for Tokenization-Free Character Language Modeling
Experiment: Before training each dataset, build a compact train-only segment lexicon by counting token n-grams of lengths 2 through 6 from train.bin, optionally using a fixed token cap for large datasets to keep preprocessing cheap. Select the top K frequent multi-character spans above a minimum count and add all single-character tokens as fallback segment IDs. Store spans in length-descending lookup dictionaries for greedy longest-match assignment. Modify get_batch to sample block_size + max_segment_len tokens internally, return the usual X and Y, and optionally return segment_targets where each position is the longest lexicon segment beginning at the corresponding next-character target position. Extend GPTConfig with use_segment_aux, segment_vocab_size, max_segment_len, segment_aux_weight, and segment_aux_ramp_iters. In GPT.__init__, add segment_head = nn.Linear(n_embd, segment_vocab_size). In GPT.forward, keep the standard tied lm_head and next-character cross-entropy unchanged, but when segment_targets are provided during training, compute an auxiliary segment cross-entropy from the final hidden states and train with total_loss = char_loss + alpha_t * segment_loss, ramping alpha_t after warmup. Validation, generation, final_info, and inference speed remain based on the ordinary character lm_head. Add diagnostics for segment prediction accuracy, multi-character span coverage, average matched span length, and auxiliary parameter overhead. Compare the baseline against K values such as 256, 1024, and 4096, plus ablations with max_segment_len 4 versus 6, across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8.

Name: gated_ngram_logit_prior
Title: Gated Log-Linear N-Gram Priors for Hybrid Character Language Modeling
Experiment: Before training each dataset, build train-only smoothed backoff n-gram continuation tables from train.bin, using orders up to 3 as the main setting and order 5 as a small ablation. Add a helper that receives the current batch X and returns centered prior_log_probs of shape batch by time by vocab, where each position uses only the visible prefix tokens in X to query the highest available n-gram context and subtracts the uniform log probability baseline. Extend GPTConfig with use_ngram_logit_prior, ngram_prior_order, and ngram_gate_bias. In GPT.__init__, add prior_gate_head = nn.Linear(n_embd, 1), initialized with a negative bias so training starts close to the neural-only baseline. In GPT.forward, compute the usual lm_head logits, and when prior_log_probs are provided, form final_logits = neural_logits + sigmoid(prior_gate_head(hidden)) * prior_log_probs. Compute the normal cross-entropy on final_logits while also reporting neural-only loss as a diagnostic. Modify estimate_loss to report combined validation loss, neural-only validation loss, and prior-only validation loss. Modify generation so that, when enabled, it queries the same causal n-gram prior from the generated prefix and samples from the gated combined logits; also run neural-only sampling as a control. Compare the baseline, fixed scalar prior weights, and learned per-token gates across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8. Report best combined validation loss, neural-only validation loss, convergence speed, total train time, inference tokens per second with prior lookup, generated samples, average gate value, gate value versus n-gram confidence, and whether the neural model can override high-confidence but wrong n-gram predictions.

Name: self_routed_adapters
Title: Self-Routed Low-Rank Adapters for Token-Conditional Autoregressive Computation
Experiment: Extend GPTConfig with use_routed_adapters, routed_adapter_layers, num_experts, adapter_rank, router_balance_weight, and router_ramp_iters. Add a SelfRoutedAdapters module with a router Linear(n_embd, num_experts) and a small bank of low-rank residual adapters, each implemented as Linear(n_embd, adapter_rank), GELU, Linear(adapter_rank, n_embd). Initialize the final adapter projections with a very small standard deviation so the model starts close to the baseline while still allowing router gradients. Modify Block to optionally add x = x + routed_adapters(ln_adapter(x)) after the standard MLP residual in selected layers. Use dense softmax router weights over all experts, and return a simple load-balancing loss that penalizes deviation of the mean router probability from uniform. In GPT.forward, accumulate router losses and, during training, add a ramped router_balance_weight term to the ordinary next-character cross-entropy. Keep estimate_loss, validation, final reporting, and generation unchanged except that routed adapters remain active in eval. Compare the baseline, a parameter-matched single shared adapter control, routed adapters in upper-half layers, and routed adapters in all layers using num_experts=4 and adapter_rank=64 as the main setting. Report best validation loss, convergence speed, total train time, inference tokens per second, parameter overhead, generated samples, router utilization entropy, and expert usage by character category and token-loss quantile across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8.

Name: multi_hash_suffix_fingerprints
Title: Multi-Hash Causal Suffix Fingerprints for Order-Aware Autoregressive Representations
Experiment: Add a lightweight training-only auxiliary objective that asks final hidden states to predict compact ordered fingerprints of the strictly previous context. Extend GPTConfig with use_suffix_fingerprints, suffix_fingerprint_windows, suffix_fingerprint_buckets, suffix_fingerprint_hashes, suffix_fingerprint_loss_weight, and suffix_fingerprint_ramp_iters. In GPT.__init__, add one small Linear(n_embd, suffix_fingerprint_buckets) head for each window-hash pair, using windows [8, 32, 128], 512 buckets, and 2 independent hash functions as the main setting. Modify GPT.forward to optionally return final hidden states while preserving the standard lm_head and next-character cross-entropy. During training, build targets from idx only: for each position t and window W, compute deterministic rolling hashes of idx[:, t-W:t] modulo suffix_fingerprint_buckets, using ignore_index for positions with fewer than W previous tokens. Compute auxiliary cross-entropy losses from the fingerprint heads and optimize total_loss = next_token_loss + alpha_t * mean(fingerprint_losses), ramping alpha_t from 0 to suffix_fingerprint_loss_weight after warmup_iters. Keep estimate_loss, clean validation, final reporting, generation, and inference speed based on the ordinary next-character lm_head for comparability. Add diagnostics for fingerprint accuracy by window, clean validation loss, cropped-context validation losses at 64 and 128 tokens, parameter overhead, and whether order-fingerprint predictability correlates with improved language modeling. Compare the baseline against suffix_fingerprint_loss_weight values 0.02, 0.05, and 0.1, plus ablations using one hash function, only short windows [8, 32], or only the long window [128], across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8.

Name: causal_lz_match_prediction
Title: Causal Lempel-Ziv Match Prediction for Compression-Aware Language Modeling
Experiment: Add a bounded training-only auxiliary objective that predicts a coarse longest-previous-match length for the upcoming continuation. Extend GPTConfig with use_lz_match_aux, lz_max_match_len, lz_context_window, lz_num_anchors, lz_loss_interval, lz_loss_weight, and lz_ramp_iters. Modify GPT.forward to optionally return final hidden states after ln_f while preserving the standard lm_head logits and next-character cross-entropy. In GPT.__init__, add lz_match_head = nn.Linear(n_embd, 6), with buckets 0, 1, 2, 3-4, 5-8, and 9+. Add a compute_lz_match_labels helper used in the training loop after warmup. On active auxiliary iterations, sample up to lz_num_anchors valid batch-time positions with enough future tokens available. For each anchor t, form the true future continuation from Y[:, t:t+lz_max_match_len], scan only the visible causal prefix X[:, max(0, t-lz_context_window):t+1] for the longest prefix match, cap the length at lz_max_match_len, and convert it to a bucket label. Train with total_loss = next_token_loss + alpha_t * lz_match_cross_entropy, ramping alpha_t from 0 to lz_loss_weight. Keep estimate_loss, clean validation, generation, final reporting, and inference speed based only on ordinary next-character loss. Add diagnostics for LZ bucket accuracy, bucket distribution, validation loss stratified by match-length bucket, copyable-versus-novel token loss, generated repeated n-gram rates, and simple generated-text compression ratio. Compare the baseline against lz_loss_weight values 0.02, 0.05, and 0.1 with lz_context_window values 64 and 128 across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8.

Name: masked_associative_recall
Title: Masked Associative Recall Augmentation for In-Context Binding in Character Language Models
Experiment: Add a training-only auxiliary associative-recall task using only token IDs from the current dataset vocabulary. Implement make_associative_recall_batch(data, vocab_size, block_size, batch_size, num_pairs, key_len, value_len, filler_len) that builds fixed-layout sequences containing several key-value records, distracting filler sampled from train.bin, and later key queries followed by their associated values. Construct recall targets with -1 everywhere except positions where the model must predict the value tokens after a query key, reusing the existing cross_entropy ignore_index behavior. In the training loop, keep the ordinary text batch and next-character loss as the primary objective. After warmup_iters, with probability recall_prob run one auxiliary recall batch and optimize total_loss = lm_loss + alpha_t * recall_loss, ramping alpha_t after warmup. Keep ordinary validation, generation, final reporting, and inference speed unchanged. Add a no-gradient recall evaluation varying num_pairs, key_len, value_len, filler distance, and distractor keys, reporting masked recall loss and exact full-value recovery accuracy. Compare against the baseline across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8 using best natural validation loss, convergence speed, total train time, inference tokens per second, generated samples, and associative recall accuracy. Main setting: num_pairs=8, key_len=3, value_len=4, recall_prob=0.1, alpha=0.2, with small ablations alpha=0.1 and recall_prob=0.05.

Name: single_edit_consistency
Title: Single-Edit Consistency for Alignment-Robust Autoregressive Language Models
Experiment: Keep the GPT architecture, clean next-character objective, validation, and generation unchanged. Add a helper make_single_edit_batch(X, vocab_size, edit_prob, edit_prefix_len) that, independently for each example, either leaves the sequence unchanged or applies one random insertion or deletion inside the first edit_prefix_len tokens. The helper crops or pads back to block_size and returns X_edit, an alignment map where each edited timestep points to the clean timestep with the same current token, and a validity mask. In the training loop, compute the standard clean forward pass on X,Y and optimize ordinary cross-entropy as the primary loss. After warmup_iters, ramp edit_prob and alpha_t over 1000 iterations, run a second forward pass on X_edit, gather detached clean logits using the alignment map, and add temperature-scaled KL consistency only on valid aligned positions after edit_prefix_len + burn_in. Use edit_prefix_len=128, burn_in=16, temperature=2.0, alpha=0.05 as the main setting, with alpha=0.1 and max edit_prob values 0.02 and 0.05 as small ablations. Add validation probes that apply insertion-only, deletion-only, and mixed single edits to validation batches, reporting aligned suffix cross-entropy, clean-to-edited KL, and robustness gap. Compare against the baseline across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8 using clean best validation loss, edit-corrupted validation loss, convergence speed, total train time, inference tokens per second, generated samples, and insertion-versus-deletion sensitivity.

Name: teacher_forced_continuation_decoder

Name: future_token_survival

Name: rare_context_tempering
Title: Rare-Context Target Tempering for Memorization-Resistant Character Language Models
Experiment: Before training each dataset, build a train-only fixed-size hash table of clipped support counts for causal context suffixes of length L, using rolling hashes over train.bin and no validation data. In get_batch or the training loop, estimate the support count for each batch-time position from the visible context suffix ending at the current input token, ignoring positions with fewer than L visible tokens. Modify GPT.forward or the training loop to compute per-token cross-entropy with reduction='none' and log probabilities. After warmup_iters, convert support counts into a per-position smoothing value epsilon_t = epsilon_max * max(0, support_threshold - count) / support_threshold, so rare contexts receive stronger smoothing and frequent contexts remain nearly baseline. Train with loss = mean((1 - epsilon_t) * one_hot_nll + epsilon_t * uniform_nll), where uniform_nll is the negative mean log probability over the vocabulary. Keep estimate_loss, best validation loss, final reporting, inference speed, and generation based on ordinary one-hot next-character loss for comparability. Compare the baseline, fixed uniform label smoothing, and rare-context tempering with L in {8, 16}, support_threshold values such as 2 and 4, and epsilon_max in {0.05, 0.1, 0.2} across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8. Name: matched_context_advantage
Title: Position-Matched Context Advantage Prediction for Selective Autoregressive Context Use
Experiment: Modify GPT.forward to optionally return final hidden states and per-token cross-entropy losses by using F.cross_entropy(..., reduction='none') reshaped to batch by time. Also add an optional position_offset argument so a cropped suffix can reuse the same learned absolute position indices as it had inside the full block. Extend GPTConfig with use_context_advantage_head, context_advantage_weight, context_advantage_ramp_iters, context_probe_len, context_advantage_interval, and context_advantage_scale. After warmup_iters and only every context_advantage_interval iterations, run a no-gradient cropped-context probe on X[:, -context_probe_len:] and Y[:, -context_probe_len:] using position_offset=block_size-context_probe_len. Align this probe with the final context_probe_len positions of the full-context pass and define a detached target advantage as clamp((nll_short - nll_full) / context_advantage_scale, 0, 1), so only positions where longer context improves true-token likelihood receive high targets. Add diagnostics for context-advantage prediction error, average predicted advantage by position and token-loss quantile, validation loss stratified by predicted advantage, and cropped-context validation losses at 64 and 128 tokens with matched position offsets. Name: causal_manifold_mixup
Title: Causal Manifold Mixup for Smooth Autoregressive Prefix Representations
Experiment: Modify GPT.forward to support optional hidden-state mixup arguments: mix_layer, mix_perm, and mix_lambda. During the forward pass, after embeddings when mix_layer=0 or after the selected Transformer block otherwise, replace hidden states h with mix_lambda * h + (1 - mix_lambda) * h[mix_perm]. When targets are provided for this mixed pass, compute a soft-label next-character loss as mix_lambda * CE(logits, targets) + (1 - mix_lambda) * CE(logits, targets[mix_perm]), preserving ignore_index behavior. In the training loop, keep the ordinary clean next-character cross-entropy as the primary objective. After warmup_iters, ramp an auxiliary weight alpha_t and run one additional mixed forward pass using a random batch permutation and lambda sampled from Beta(mixup_beta, mixup_beta), optionally converted to max(lambda, 1-lambda) to avoid overly ambiguous blends. Use a fixed middle layer such as mix_layer=3 as the main setting, with simple ablations at mix_layer=0 and mix_layer=6. Keep estimate_loss, clean validation, generation, final reporting, and inference speed based on the ordinary unmixed model. Compare against the baseline across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8 using best clean validation loss, convergence speed, total train time, inference tokens per second, generated samples, confidence calibration, and validation loss under the same hidden-state mixup diagnostic. Main settings: mixup_beta in {0.2, 0.4} and auxiliary weight alpha in {0.1, 0.25}.

Name: causal_transition_cache
Title: Causal Transition Caches for In-Context Analogical Language Modeling
Experiment: Add an optional strictly causal transition-cache output path to GPT. Extend GPTConfig with use_transition_cache, transition_cache_window, transition_cache_temperature, and transition_cache_gate_bias. In GPT.__init__, add query and key projections from final hidden states plus a scalar gate head initialized with a negative bias so training begins close to the baseline. In GPT.forward, compute the ordinary lm_head logits and next-character cross-entropy as usual. When the transition cache is enabled, for each prediction position t compare its query hidden state only to earlier key states s where s < t and t - s <= transition_cache_window. Associate each earlier key position s with the visible continuation token idx[:, s + 1], which avoids target leakage because s + 1 <= t. Softmax the masked similarities over valid earlier transitions, scatter-add the mass into a vocabulary-sized cache distribution, and blend this cache distribution with the neural softmax distribution using sigmoid(gate_head(hidden_t)). Force the cache gate to zero at positions with no valid earlier transition. Compute training and validation negative log likelihood from the blended probabilities, while also logging neural-only loss, cache-only loss on valid positions, average gate value, target-in-cache rate, and cache confidence. For generation, compute the same cache from the generated prefix and return log blended probabilities for the final position so the existing sampling code remains usable. Compare the baseline against transition_cache_window values 32, 64, and 128, plus a fixed-gate ablation, across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8. Report best blended validation loss, neural-only validation loss, convergence speed, total train time, inference tokens per second, generated samples, gate usage, target-in-cache rate, and gains stratified by whether the true next token appeared as a prior continuation.

Name: dual_mode_span_denoising

After warmup_iters, sample short contiguous masked spans in X, replace masked token embeddings with mask_emb, set denoise_targets to X only at masked positions and -1 elsewhere, and run a second forward pass with is_causal=False and mode_id=1. Optimize total_loss = lm_loss + alpha_t * denoise_loss, ramping alpha_t to denoise_loss_weight. Use denoise_mask_prob=0.15, denoise_span_len=3, and denoise_loss_weight=0.1 as the main setting, with ablations using denoise_loss_weight=0.05, denoise_span_len=1, no mode embeddings, and a causal-denoising control where the auxiliary pass keeps is_causal=True. Name: surprisal_to_go_forecasting

Name: ecoc_target_supervision

Name: prediction_conditioned_context_bottleneck
Title: Prediction-Conditioned Context Bottlenecks for Sufficient Autoregressive Evidence
Experiment: Modify GPT.forward to optionally accept input_embeds_override and optionally return final hidden states before the lm_head while preserving standard logits, loss, validation, and generation. Use the detached clean hidden state h[:, t] as a prediction query and detached token embeddings from visible positions s <= t as keys to produce sigmoid keep gates over the causal prefix for each example. Always preserve the most recent bottleneck_preserve_recent positions before t, and replace older prefix embeddings by gate * token_emb + (1 - gate) * null_context_emb while leaving positions after t unchanged. Run one auxiliary forward pass on these masked embeddings, gather logits only at position t, and add a temperature-scaled KL consistency loss from detached clean logits[:, t] to masked logits[:, t]. Add a budget penalty encouraging the mean gate value over maskable prefix positions toward bottleneck_target_keep_rate, ramping auxiliary weights after warmup. Keep estimate_loss, best validation loss, generation, final reporting, and inference speed based on the ordinary unmasked model. Name: causal_histogram_memory

Implement build_causal_histograms(idx, vocab_size, windows), which uses one-hot encodings and cumulative sums to compute normalized visible-prefix token histograms for windows such as [16, 64, 256] at every sequence position, including only tokens available up to the current input position and never using future targets. In GPT.__init__, add a small projection module that maps the concatenated histograms to n_embd, followed by a learned scalar gate initialized near zero. In GPT.forward, when enabled, add gate * histogram_projection to the token embeddings before position embeddings and dropout.
