Name: periodic_sharpness_aware_lm
Title: Periodic Sharpness-Aware Updates for Generalizable Character Language Models
Experiment: Add an optional periodic Sharpness-Aware Minimization mode around the existing AdamW optimizer while keeping the GPT architecture, data loader, validation, generation, and next-character objective unchanged. During warmup_iters, train exactly as the baseline. After warmup, every sam_interval iterations, compute the ordinary loss and scaled gradients on the current batch, unscale gradients, estimate the global gradient norm over optimizer parameters, perturb parameters by rho * grad / grad_norm, clear gradients, run a second forward/backward pass on the same batch, restore the original parameters, then apply the existing gradient clipping, AdamW step, and GradScaler update. On non-SAM iterations, use the baseline update. Compare baseline AdamW against periodic SAM with rho values 0.02 and 0.05 and sam_interval values 4 and 8, plus full SAM on shakespeare_char and a compute-aware control that performs an extra forward/backward pass without perturbing weights. Keep final reporting and inference speed unchanged. Add diagnostics for best validation loss, train-validation gap, gradient norm, perturbation norm, convergence speed, total training time, validation loss under shorter contexts 64 and 128, validation loss under small input-token corruption, generated samples, and inference tokens per second across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8.

Name: causal_evidence_distillation
Title: Causal Evidence Distillation for Interpretable Autoregressive Context Use
Experiment: Modify GPT.forward to optionally return final hidden states after ln_f while preserving the standard logits, loss, validation, generation, and final reporting behavior. Add a small evidence_scorer module that projects clean hidden states to a low-dimensional space and scores an anchor position against candidate visible context positions with scaled dot products. In the training loop, keep ordinary next-character cross-entropy as the primary objective. After warmup_iters and only every evidence_interval iterations, sample a small sub-batch, one or more anchor positions t per example, and a fixed number of candidate causal positions s <= t from local, medium, and distant distance bands. From the clean forward pass, record the detached true-token negative log likelihood at each anchor. Build one batched ablation input by repeating the sampled examples and replacing exactly one candidate token per copy with a random valid token different from the original token. Run this ablation batch under torch.no_grad(), measure the increase in true-token negative log likelihood at each anchor, clamp negative increases to zero, and skip anchors whose total measured influence is near zero. Normalize the remaining candidate influences into a soft evidence target. Train evidence_scorer on the clean hidden states to predict this target with KL divergence, adding alpha_t * evidence_loss to the primary LM loss with alpha_t ramped after warmup. Keep estimate_loss, best validation loss, generation, and inference speed based only on the ordinary lm_head, with no evidence computation at inference. Add diagnostics for evidence top-k accuracy, rank correlation with measured ablation influence, average influence by distance band, validation loss stratified by predicted context dependence, target-in-context rate, and generated repetition or copy-rate metrics. Compare the baseline against evidence_loss_weight values such as 0.02, 0.05, and 0.1, evidence_interval values such as 4 and 8, and candidate counts such as 8 and 16 across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8.

Name: hindsight_reverse_distillation
Title: Hindsight Reverse-Context Distillation for Causal Character Language Models
Experiment: Extend GPTConfig with use_direction_embedding, reverse_loss_weight, hindsight_distill_weight, hindsight_temperature, hindsight_ramp_iters, hindsight_interval, and use_hindsight_confidence_weighting. Add a two-entry learned direction embedding in GPT.__init__ when enabled, and modify GPT.forward to accept direction_id, defaulting to the forward direction for validation and generation. In the training loop, keep the ordinary forward batch X,Y and forward next-character cross-entropy as the primary objective. Construct a reversed batch from the same contiguous window with X_rev = torch.flip(Y, dims=[1]) and Y_rev = torch.flip(X, dims=[1]), then train the reverse direction with a smaller auxiliary cross-entropy weight. After warmup_iters, and only every hindsight_interval iterations to limit overhead, align detached reverse logits to forward targets: reverse position T-2-t predicts the same character as forward target Y[:, t], so skip the final forward position. Add a temperature-scaled KL loss from the aligned reverse-context teacher distribution to the forward logits, optionally weighting positions by low reverse entropy. Optimize total_loss = forward_ce + reverse_loss_weight * reverse_ce + alpha_t * hindsight_temperature^2 * hindsight_KL, with alpha_t ramped after warmup. Keep estimate_loss, best validation loss, generation, final reporting, and inference speed strictly forward-direction only. Add diagnostics for reverse validation loss, forward-reverse KL, teacher entropy, validation loss stratified by teacher confidence, calibration by confidence bucket, and training-time overhead. Compare the baseline against hindsight_distill_weight values 0.03, 0.05, and 0.1, with and without confidence weighting, across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8.

Name: distance_band_sensitivity_smoothing
Title: Distance-Band Sensitivity Smoothing for Robust Autoregressive Context Use
Experiment: Modify GPT.forward to optionally accept input_embeds_override while preserving the existing logits, loss, validation, generation, and final reporting behavior. In the training loop, keep ordinary next-character cross-entropy on clean X,Y as the primary objective. After warmup_iters and every sensitivity_interval iterations, run one auxiliary consistency pass on a small sub-batch. First compute clean logits with no gradients flowing into the consistency target. Then build token embeddings for the same inputs, sample one causal prefix distance band such as 64-128 or 128-256 tokens before each prediction position, add small Gaussian embedding perturbations only inside the selected older band, and preserve the most recent preserve_recent tokens. Run the model on the perturbed embeddings and compute a temperature-scaled KL loss from detached clean logits to perturbed logits only on suffix positions whose selected band is valid. Train with total_loss = clean_loss + alpha_t * sensitivity_loss, ramping alpha_t after warmup. Keep estimate_loss, best validation loss, inference speed, and generation based on the ordinary clean model. Add diagnostics for clean validation loss, validation loss under distance-banded embedding perturbations, old-prefix token corruption, distractor-prefix replacement, sensitivity by distance band, train-validation gap, total training time, and generated samples. Compare the baseline against alpha values 0.03 and 0.1, perturbation scales 0.02 and 0.05 times embedding RMS, and preserve_recent values 32 and 64 across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8.

Name: persistent_gradient_projection
Title: Persistent Gradient Projection for Low-Noise Autoregressive Language Model Training
Experiment: Add an optional optimizer-side persistent gradient projection filter to the existing training loop. Introduce settings such as use_persistent_gradient_projection, grad_ema_beta, projection_strength, projection_ramp_iters, min_projection_cosine, and min_projected_params. After scaler.scale(loss).backward(), call scaler.unscale_(optimizer) once before gradient clipping when the filter is active. Maintain one detached slow EMA buffer per trainable parameter tensor using the current unscaled gradient. After warmup_iters, ramp projection_strength from 0 to its target value. For each sufficiently large parameter tensor, compute the cosine similarity between the current gradient g and the bias-corrected EMA direction e. If the cosine exceeds min_projection_cosine, decompose g into a parallel component along e and an orthogonal residual, then replace the gradient with g_parallel + (1 - projection_strength_t * cosine) * g_orthogonal. If the tensor is small or agreement is low, leave its gradient unchanged. Keep the GPT architecture, data loader, objective, validation, generation, and final reporting unchanged. Compare baseline AdamW against projection settings with grad_ema_beta values 0.98 and 0.995 and projection_strength values 0.25, 0.5, and 0.75 across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8. Include a simple control that adds the gradient EMA like extra momentum without orthogonal projection. Report best validation loss, convergence speed, train-validation gap, total train time, inference tokens per second, generated samples, layerwise gradient-EMA cosine agreement, and effective update norm.

Name: frequency_bucketed_cipher_consistency
Title: Frequency-Bucketed Cipher Consistency for Symbol-Robust Character Language Models
Experiment: Add a training-only frequency-bucketed substitution-cipher consistency objective. Before training, compute unigram token frequencies from train.bin and partition vocabulary IDs into a small number of frequency buckets, such as 4 or 8. Implement helpers to sample a random permutation within each bucket, apply it to X and Y, and inverse-permute logits back to the original vocabulary order. In the training loop, keep the ordinary clean forward pass and next-character cross-entropy as the primary loss. After warmup_iters, with probability p_t ramped to values such as 0.25 or 0.5, run a second forward pass on X_perm,Y_perm. Add a small auxiliary objective: permuted-target cross-entropy plus a temperature-scaled KL consistency loss between detached clean logits and inverse-permuted cipher logits at matching positions. Use auxiliary weights such as 0.05 and 0.1 so clean language modeling remains dominant. Keep estimate_loss, validation, generation, final reporting, and inference speed on the original unpermuted vocabulary. Add diagnostics for validation loss under fixed frequency-bucketed ciphers, full-random-cipher robustness as a stress test, rare-character validation loss, calibration by confidence bucket, and generated samples. Compare the baseline against bucketed cipher consistency with p=0.25 and p=0.5, plus ablations using full random ciphers and permuted cross-entropy without KL, across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8.

Name: latent_context_resets
Title: Latent Context Reset Gates for Content-Adaptive Causal Attention
Experiment: Extend GPTConfig with use_latent_context_resets, reset_strength, reset_budget_weight, target_reset_rate, reset_ramp_iters, and reset_temperature. Modify Block to include a small reset_gate_head, for example nn.Linear(n_embd, 1), applied to ln_1(x) before attention. Modify CausalSelfAttention.forward to optionally accept reset_probs and reset_strength_current. When reset gates are active, use the manual attention path and add a soft barrier penalty to causal attention logits: for query position t and key position s <= t, compute the cumulative reset probability over positions s+1 through t using cumsum(reset_probs), then add -reset_strength_current * barrier to the attention logit before softmax. Keep the ordinary next-character cross-entropy objective, optimizer, validation, generation, and sampling unchanged. In the training loop, ramp reset_strength_current from 0 to reset_strength after warmup_iters and add reset_budget_weight * (mean_reset_prob - target_reset_rate)^2 to the loss, averaging reset probabilities over layers, batch examples, and positions. Compare the baseline, a manual-attention no-reset control, learned reset gates with target_reset_rate values such as 0.02, 0.05, and 0.10, and a simple distance-decay attention control with matched average attenuation. Report best validation loss, convergence speed, total train time, inference tokens per second, generated samples, learned reset rate, reset entropy, attention mass crossing reset boundaries, cropped-context validation losses at 64 and 128 tokens, and distractor-prefix robustness across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8.

Name: orthogonal_context_factorization
Title: Orthogonal Context Factorization for Robust Character Language Modeling
Experiment: Extend GPTConfig with use_context_factorization, context_factor_dim, context_factor_loss_weight, context_orth_weight, and context_factor_ramp_iters. In GPT.__init__, add an identity-initialized predictive_adapter mapping n_embd to n_embd, a context_proj mapping n_embd to context_factor_dim, and two small auxiliary heads from the context stream: one predicts a coarse absolute position bucket and one predicts the previous-occurrence distance bucket of the current input token, both computed causally from idx only. Name: suffix_continuation_attention_bias
Title: Causal Suffix-Continuation Attention Biases for In-Context Character Retrieval
Experiment: Add an optional strictly causal suffix-continuation bias to attention. Extend GPTConfig with use_suffix_continuation_bias, suffix_match_max_len, suffix_match_window, and suffix_bias_scale. Implement build_suffix_continuation_bias(idx, max_len, window), returning an additive attention bias where query position t receives positive bias toward key position c only when c < t and the suffix ending at t matches the earlier suffix ending at c - 1; the key c is therefore the visible continuation that followed the earlier matching context. Normalize match length by max_len, mask out invalid/self/future positions, and compute the bias once per forward pass from idx only. Modify CausalSelfAttention.forward to accept this bias and use the manual attention path when enabled, adding per-layer per-head learned scalar gates initialized to zero so training starts as the baseline. Keep the ordinary next-character cross-entropy objective, optimizer, estimate_loss, generation, and final reporting unchanged. Compare the flash-attention baseline, a manual-attention no-bias control, and suffix-continuation bias variants with max_len values 4 and 8 and windows 64 and 128 across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8. Report best validation loss, convergence speed, total train time, inference tokens per second, learned gate values, attention mass on matched continuations, validation loss stratified by whether a matching suffix continuation exists, and generated repetition/copy diagnostics.

Name: causal_replaced_token_detection
Title: Causal Replaced-Token Detection for Exposure-Robust Character Language Models
Experiment: Add a training-only causal replaced-token detection auxiliary task. Extend GPTConfig with use_replaced_token_detection, rtd_loss_weight, rtd_corruption_prob, rtd_ramp_iters, rtd_temperature, rtd_top_k, and rtd_interval. Modify GPT.__init__ to add rtd_head = nn.Linear(n_embd, 1), and modify GPT.forward to optionally return final hidden states after ln_f while preserving the ordinary logits, loss, validation, generation, and final reporting behavior. In the training loop, compute the standard clean forward pass on X,Y and optimize ordinary next-character cross-entropy as the primary loss. After warmup_iters and only every rtd_interval iterations, use detached clean logits from positions 0 through T-2 to sample plausible replacements for X[:, 1:], since logit position t-1 causally predicts input token X[:, t]. Apply optional top-k truncation and temperature, avoid replacing a token with itself, and replace eligible positions with probability ramped up to rtd_corruption_prob. Run a second forward pass on X_corrupt for hidden states only, predict the binary replacement mask from rtd_head(hidden_corrupt), and add a balanced BCEWithLogits loss: total_loss = clean_ce_loss + alpha_t * rtd_loss. Do not apply next-token cross-entropy to corrupted inputs. Keep estimate_loss, best validation loss, generation, final_info, and inference speed based only on the clean lm_head. Add diagnostics for RTD accuracy/AUROC, clean validation loss, validation loss under model-sampled corrupted prefixes, train-time overhead, and generated repetition metrics. Compare the baseline against rtd_corruption_prob values 0.05 and 0.10 with rtd_loss_weight values 0.05 and 0.1, plus a simple ablation using uniform random replacements instead of model-sampled near misses across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8.

Name: causal_fast_weight_memory
Title: Causal Fast-Weight Memories for Content-Addressed Autoregressive State
Experiment: Add an optional residual fast-weight memory branch to selected Transformer blocks. Extend GPTConfig with use_fast_weight_memory, fast_weight_layers, fast_weight_key_dim, fast_weight_value_dim, fast_weight_gate_init, and fast_weight_decay. Implement a CausalFastWeightMemory module that projects normalized hidden states to queries, keys, and values, applies a positive feature map such as elu(x)+1 to queries and keys, builds an exclusive causal prefix memory by cumulatively summing key-value outer products from positions strictly before the current position, retrieves with normalized linear attention, projects the retrieved value back to n_embd, and applies dropout. In Block.__init__, add ln_fast, fast_memory, and a learnable scalar gate logit initialized so sigmoid(gate) is near fast_weight_gate_init, for example 0.05. In Block.forward, insert x = x + sigmoid(fast_gate) * fast_memory(ln_fast(x)) after attention and before the MLP for enabled layers. Keep the standard next-character cross-entropy objective, optimizer, validation, generation, and final reporting unchanged. Report best validation loss, convergence speed, total train time, inference tokens per second, parameter overhead, learned gate values, generated samples, and validation loss stratified by whether the target token previously appeared in the visible context. The hypothesis is that a small internal content-addressed memory improves recurrence-sensitive prediction and in-context binding without requiring an output-time cache or external data.

Name: ambiguous_suffix_negatives
Title: Ambiguous Suffix Negatives for Long-Context Disambiguation
Experiment: Before training each dataset, build a train-only ambiguous suffix table from train.bin. For suffix lengths such as 4 and 8, map each observed suffix to its most frequent next-character continuations, and keep only suffixes with at least two distinct continuations. Keep the GPT architecture, optimizer, validation, generation, and ordinary next-character cross-entropy unchanged. In the training loop, after warmup_iters and every suffix_negative_interval iterations, sample a bounded number of batch-time positions. For each position, look up the longest available suffix ending at the current input token, choose up to k locally plausible alternative continuations from the suffix table excluding the true target, and compute an auxiliary candidate-set contrastive loss over the full-context logits: cross-entropy where the candidates are the true next token plus the sampled suffix-matched negatives. Train with total_loss = next_token_loss + alpha_t * suffix_negative_loss, ramping alpha_t after warmup. Keep estimate_loss and final reporting based on ordinary validation cross-entropy. Add diagnostics for suffix-table coverage, valid negative positions per batch, candidate-set accuracy, validation loss stratified by ambiguous versus unambiguous suffixes, cropped-context validation losses at 64 and 128 tokens, total train time, inference tokens per second, and generated samples. Compare the baseline against suffix lengths [4], [8], and [4,8], negative counts k in {1,4}, and contrast weights 0.02, 0.05, and 0.1 across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8.

Name: predictive_state_distillation
Title: Train-Only Predictive State Distillation for Character Language Models
Experiment: Before training each dataset, scan train.bin only and count suffix-to-next-character statistics for causal context lengths 1 through 5. Retain only suffixes above a minimum count threshold, capped to the most frequent contexts for enwik8 and text8. Convert each retained suffix into a smoothed top-k continuation probability vector over the dataset vocabulary, then cluster these vectors into num_predictive_states empirical predictive states using simple NumPy k-means. Store a mapping from each retained suffix to its cluster ID. Extend GPTConfig with use_predictive_state_aux, num_predictive_states, predictive_state_loss_weight, predictive_state_ramp_iters, max_state_context_len, and min_state_context_count. Add predictive_state_head = nn.Linear(n_embd, num_predictive_states) in GPT.__init__, and modify GPT.forward to optionally return final hidden states while preserving the standard lm_head logits and ordinary next-character cross-entropy. In the training loop, build predictive_state_targets for each batch position by looking up the longest retained visible suffix ending at the current input token, using ignore_index when no reliable suffix is found. After warmup_iters, ramp alpha_t to predictive_state_loss_weight and optimize total_loss = next_token_loss + alpha_t * predictive_state_cross_entropy. Keep estimate_loss, best validation loss, generation, final_info, and inference speed based only on ordinary next-character prediction. Add diagnostics for state-target coverage, predictive-state accuracy, validation loss on covered versus uncovered contexts, validation loss on rare contexts, and cluster entropy. Compare the baseline against num_predictive_states values such as 64, 128, and 256 with predictive_state_loss_weight values 0.02 and 0.05 across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8.

Name: elastic_structured_pruning
Title: Elastic Structured Pruning Distillation for Width-Robust Character Transformers
Experiment: Add optional nested structured width masks to the Transformer while keeping tensor shapes unchanged. Extend GPTConfig with use_elastic_pruning, elastic_width_choices, elastic_distill_weight, elastic_ce_weight, elastic_temperature, elastic_ramp_iters, and elastic_interval. In each attention and MLP module, create fixed random nested mask orders so smaller subnetworks keep consistent per-layer subsets without always favoring low-index heads or channels. Modify CausalSelfAttention.forward to accept an optional head_keep_frac and zero inactive attention heads before reassembling the head outputs. Modify MLP.forward to accept an optional mlp_keep_frac and zero inactive intermediate channels after GELU and before the output projection. In GPT.forward and Block.forward, accept width_mult and pass the corresponding keep fractions through all layers, with width_mult=1.0 exactly reproducing the baseline. In the training loop, compute the ordinary full-width forward pass and standard next-character cross-entropy. After warmup_iters, every elastic_interval iterations, sample width_mult from values such as [0.5, 0.75], run a second masked forward pass on the same batch, and add a ramped auxiliary loss combining temperature-scaled KL distillation from detached full-width logits to masked logits plus a small masked-subnetwork cross-entropy term. Report best full-width validation loss, masked-subnetwork validation losses, degradation relative to full width, convergence speed, total train time, generated samples, robustness to structured pruning, and a theoretical compute proxy based on active heads and MLP channels across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8.

Name: lag_queried_past_recall
Title: Lag-Queried Past Recall for Addressable Causal Context Representations
Experiment: Add a sparse training-only auxiliary objective that asks each final hidden state to recover earlier input tokens when queried by a relative lag. Extend GPTConfig with use_past_recall, past_recall_lags, past_recall_anchors, past_recall_loss_weight, and past_recall_ramp_iters. In GPT.__init__, add a learned lag embedding table for lags such as [2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64, 128], a small MLP that combines hidden_t with the selected lag embedding, and a past_recall_head projecting to vocab_size. Modify GPT.forward to optionally return final hidden states after ln_f while preserving the standard lm_head logits and next-character cross-entropy behavior. During training after warmup_iters, sample a bounded number of valid anchor-lag pairs with t >= lag, use idx[:, t - lag] as the target, and compute cross-entropy from the lag-conditioned recall head. Balance the sampled pairs across short, medium, and long lags so nearby tokens do not dominate. Optimize total_loss = next_token_loss + alpha_t * past_recall_loss, ramping alpha_t to past_recall_loss_weight. Keep estimate_loss, clean validation, generation, final_info, and inference speed based only on ordinary next-character prediction. Add diagnostics for recall accuracy by lag, validation loss stratified by whether the next token appeared in the recent context, cropped-context validation losses at 64 and 128 tokens, generated repetition/copy metrics, and auxiliary parameter overhead. Compare the baseline against multi-scale lags [2,4,8,16,32,64,128], short-only lags [2,4,8,16], long-only lags [32,64,128], and a shuffled-lag-target control with loss weights 0.02 and 0.05 across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8.

Name: future_spectral_codes
Title: Future Spectral Code Prediction for Ordered Long-Horizon Autoregressive Supervision
Experiment: Add a training-only auxiliary objective that asks each hidden state to predict a compact ordered sketch of its near-future continuation. Extend GPTConfig with use_future_spectral_codes, spectral_window, spectral_code_dim, spectral_num_coeffs, spectral_loss_weight, spectral_ramp_iters, and spectral_sample_positions. In GPT.__init__, register two frozen buffers when enabled: a deterministic random token-code table of shape vocab_size by spectral_code_dim, normalized per token, and a fixed DCT basis over spectral_window future offsets, keeping only the first spectral_num_coeffs low-frequency coefficients. Add future_spectral_head = nn.Linear(n_embd, spectral_num_coeffs * spectral_code_dim). In GPT.forward, keep the standard lm_head and next-character cross-entropy unchanged. Optimize total_loss = next_token_loss + alpha_t * spectral_loss, where alpha_t ramps from 0 to spectral_loss_weight after warmup_iters. Add diagnostics for spectral prediction error by coefficient index, parameter overhead, and generated repetition rates. Compare the baseline against spectral_window values 16 and 32, spectral_num_coeffs values 4 and 8, and spectral_loss_weight values 0.02 and 0.05 across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8. Include an unordered future-code averaging ablation to test whether ordered spectral structure is useful.

Name: gated_causal_context_norm
Title: Gated Causal Context Normalization for Prefix-Relative Autoregressive Representations
Experiment: Extend GPTConfig with use_causal_context_norm, context_norm_window, context_norm_layers, context_norm_gate_init, and context_norm_eps. Implement a CausalContextNorm module that receives hidden states of shape B by T by C and computes per-feature causal mean and variance using only visible positions up to each timestep. Support either full-prefix statistics or a fixed recent window using cumulative sums, with a variance floor for early-token stability. In Block.__init__, add an optional LayerNorm, the CausalContextNorm module, a Linear projection back to n_embd, dropout, and a learnable scalar gate initialized to a small value such as 0.01. In Block.forward, insert the branch after attention and before the MLP: x = x + gate * dropout(proj(causal_context_norm(ln_ctx(x)))). Keep the standard next-character cross-entropy objective, optimizer, validation, generation, and final reporting unchanged. Compare the baseline against causal context normalization in all layers and in only the lower half of layers, using full-prefix statistics and a fixed window such as 128. Report best validation loss, convergence speed, total training time, inference tokens per second, generated samples, parameter overhead, learned gate values, activation variance diagnostics, and cropped-context validation losses at 64 and 128 tokens across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8.

Name: dropout_stress_consistency
Title: Dropout Stress Consistency for Subnetwork-Robust Autoregressive Language Models
Experiment: Add a training-only consistency regularizer between a normal dropout forward pass and a stronger dropout stress forward pass of the same clean batch. Modify GPT.forward, Block.forward, CausalSelfAttention.forward, and MLP.forward to accept an optional dropout_scale argument that temporarily multiplies existing dropout probabilities, capped below 1.0, while leaving eval-mode behavior unchanged. In the training loop, compute the ordinary forward pass on X,Y with dropout_scale=1.0 and optimize its standard next-character cross-entropy as the primary loss. After warmup_iters, run a second forward pass on the same X,Y with dropout_scale values such as 1.5 or 2.0. Add a temperature-scaled KL loss from the detached normal-pass distribution to the stressed-pass distribution, weighted per token by detached confidence from the normal pass, for example 1 minus normalized entropy, with weights normalized to mean 1 over valid positions. Ramp the consistency weight from 0 to alpha over 1000 iterations after warmup. Keep estimate_loss, best validation loss, final_info, generation, and inference speed based on the ordinary eval-mode model with no dropout. Add diagnostics for normal-versus-stressed agreement, validation calibration, MC-dropout validation loss, and validation loss under forced dropout stress. Compare the baseline against alpha values 0.03 and 0.1 with dropout_scale values 1.5 and 2.0, plus an unweighted consistency ablation, across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8.

Name: successor_distribution_td
Title: Temporal-Difference Successor Distributions for Autoregressive Representation Learning
Experiment: Extend GPTConfig with use_successor_distribution, successor_gammas, successor_loss_weight, and successor_ramp_iters. In GPT.__init__, add one linear successor head per discount factor, mapping final hidden states after ln_f to vocab_size logits. Modify GPT.forward to optionally return successor logits while preserving the standard lm_head logits and ordinary next-character cross-entropy behavior. In the training loop, keep next-token cross-entropy as the primary loss. After warmup_iters, ramp the auxiliary weight and train each successor head with a detached Bellman-style target: for positions 0 through T-2, target_dist = (1 - gamma) * one_hot(targets[:, t]) + gamma * softmax(successor_logits[:, t + 1]).detach(), and minimize soft cross-entropy from successor_logits[:, t] to this target. Use the immediate one-hot target or ignore_index handling for tail positions. Keep estimate_loss, best validation loss, generation, final reporting, and inference speed based only on the ordinary lm_head. Add diagnostics for successor TD loss, successor entropy, agreement with empirical finite-window future histograms, and validation loss stratified by whether the next token recurs soon. Compare the baseline against successor_gammas=[0.8] and [0.5, 0.9] with successor_loss_weight values 0.02 and 0.05 across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8.

Name: output_substitution_laplacian
Title: Train-Derived Output Substitution Geometry for Character Language Models
Experiment: Before training each dataset, scan train.bin only and build a sparse character substitution graph. For each target character, accumulate counts of hashed causal suffix contexts of lengths 1 through 4 that preceded it. Convert these counts into smoothed, frequency-corrected context vectors, for example using log count ratios or positive PMI-style weighting, and ignore characters below a small minimum count threshold. Compute cosine similarities between normalized character context vectors, keep top-k neighbors per character such as k=4 or k=8, and symmetrize the resulting weighted graph. Keep the GPT architecture, data loader, ordinary next-character cross-entropy, validation, generation, and final reporting unchanged. During training, after warmup_iters, add a ramped degree-normalized Laplacian regularizer on the tied lm_head rows: for each graph edge i,j with weight s_ij, penalize s_ij * ||normalize(w_i) - normalize(w_j)||^2, scaled by small weights such as 1e-4, 3e-4, and 1e-3. Compare against the baseline and controls using random neighbors, unigram-frequency neighbors, and an unsymmetrized graph. Report best validation loss, convergence speed, train-validation gap, rare-character validation loss, generated samples, output-neighbor alignment with the train-derived graph, and inference tokens per second across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8.

Name: predictive_information_bottleneck
Title: Predictive Information Bottlenecks for Compressible Autoregressive States
Experiment: Modify GPT.forward to optionally return final hidden states after ln_f while preserving the standard logits and next-character cross-entropy behavior. Extend GPTConfig with use_predictive_bottleneck, bottleneck_dim, bottleneck_loss_weight, bottleneck_kl_weight, bottleneck_kl_free_bits, bottleneck_sample_positions, and bottleneck_ramp_iters. In GPT.__init__, add a compact auxiliary bottleneck module: LayerNorm, Linear(n_embd, 2 * bottleneck_dim) producing mu and logvar, Linear(bottleneck_dim, n_embd) decoding back to n_embd, and an optional LayerNorm before reusing the existing tied lm_head. During training after warmup_iters, sample a bounded number of batch-time positions, draw z with the reparameterization trick, decode z, and compute auxiliary next-character cross-entropy through the tied lm_head on the corresponding targets. Add a ramped free-bits KL penalty such as mean(relu(KL_per_token - bottleneck_kl_free_bits)) so the latent is compressed without strongly encouraging collapse. Optimize total_loss = next_token_loss + alpha_t * bottleneck_ce + beta_t * kl_budget_loss. Keep estimate_loss, best validation loss, final reporting, generation, and inference speed based only on the ordinary lm_head. Add diagnostics for deterministic bottleneck validation loss using mu, KL per token, active latent dimensions, train-validation gap, and calibration by confidence bucket. Compare bottleneck_dim values 64, 128, and 256 with bottleneck_loss_weight values 0.05 and 0.1 across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8, including controls with a deterministic low-rank bottleneck and with KL disabled.

Name: soft_tied_output_embeddings
Title: Soft-Tied Output Embeddings for Flexible Character Language Modeling
Experiment: Modify GPT to support three output-embedding modes: hard tied, untied, and soft low-rank tied. Extend GPTConfig with output_tie_mode, output_delta_rank, and output_delta_l2_weight. For output_tie_mode='hard', keep the existing tied embedding behavior. For output_tie_mode='untied', use an independent lm_head as a simple capacity control. For output_tie_mode='soft_low_rank', compute logits with W_out = W_in + A @ B, where W_in is the input embedding table, A has shape vocab_size by output_delta_rank, B has shape output_delta_rank by n_embd, A is small-random initialized, and B is zero-initialized so training begins exactly at the hard-tied model. Add a small training-only L2 penalty on A @ B to keep the residual correction controlled, while validation loss remains ordinary next-character cross-entropy. Route all output logits through a helper so generation, validation, optimizer setup, and final reporting remain otherwise unchanged. Compare hard tied, untied, and soft-low-rank variants with ranks 4, 8, 16, and 32 across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8. Report best validation loss, convergence speed, total train time, inference tokens per second, parameter overhead, residual norm, input-output embedding cosine similarity, rare-character validation loss, and generated samples.

Name: boundary_rewindow_consistency
Title: Boundary Re-Windowing Consistency for Fixed-Context Autoregressive Training
Experiment: Add a get_rewindow_batch helper that samples a raw span of length block_size + offset + 1, where offset is sampled from values such as 32, 64, and 128. Construct two overlapping views: X_base,Y_base from the first block_size tokens and X_shift,Y_shift from the span starting at offset. Base logits at positions offset:block_size align with shifted logits at positions 0:block_size-offset because they predict the same next characters from different window boundaries. Keep the ordinary next-character cross-entropy on X_base,Y_base as the primary objective. After warmup_iters and every rewindow_interval iterations, run the shifted view as an auxiliary forward pass and add a temperature-scaled KL consistency loss from detached base-view logits to shifted-view logits on aligned positions, ignoring the first burn_in shifted positions and weighting by detached base-view confidence. Ramp the consistency weight to alpha values such as 0.03, 0.05, and 0.1. Keep validation, generation, final reporting, and inference speed unchanged. Add diagnostics for clean validation loss, overlap KL at fixed offsets, validation loss by absolute block position, and true-token NLL gaps between base and shifted views. Compare against the baseline across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8 using best validation loss, convergence speed, total training time, inference tokens per second, generated samples, and boundary-robustness diagnostics.

Name: zero_init_relative_bias
Title: Zero-Initialized Learned Relative Distance Biases for Small Character Transformers
Experiment: Extend GPTConfig with position_encoding choices such as 'absolute', 'relative_bias', and 'absolute_relative_bias', plus relative_num_buckets and relative_max_distance. Modify CausalSelfAttention to optionally use the manual attention path and add a learned per-head relative-distance bias table to causal attention logits before softmax. Build a T by T causal distance matrix query_index - key_index, map distances into exact buckets for small lags and logarithmic buckets for larger lags, and look up a bias table of shape n_head by relative_num_buckets. Initialize the relative bias table to zero so training begins exactly at the corresponding no-relative-bias model while gradients still flow into the table. In GPT.forward, use learned absolute position embeddings only for variants whose position_encoding includes 'absolute'. Keep the standard next-character cross-entropy objective, optimizer, validation, generation, and final reporting unchanged. Compare the original flash-attention absolute baseline, a manual-attention absolute control, relative-bias-only, and absolute+relative variants across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8. Report best validation loss, convergence speed, total training time, inference tokens per second, parameter overhead, cropped-context validation losses at 64 and 128 tokens, learned relative-bias magnitudes, and learned distance-bias curves by layer and head.

Name: first_order_prefix_meta_adapters
Title: First-Order Prefix Meta-Adaptation for Locally Nonstationary Character Language Models
Experiment: Add optional low-rank residual adapters to Transformer blocks, for example after the MLP residual, with zero-initialized output projections so training starts close to the baseline. Keep the ordinary next-character cross-entropy on full 256-token training batches as the primary objective. After warmup_iters and every meta_interval iterations, create a self-supervised adaptation episode by splitting each batch into a 128-token prefix and a 128-token suffix. Compute prefix loss using only the prefix tokens, take one first-order SGD update on adapter parameters only, then run a suffix forward pass with the temporary adapted adapter parameters and add alpha_t * suffix_meta_loss to the ordinary LM loss. Implement this with torch.func.functional_call or a small adapter fast-weight override path, treating the inner update as first-order and disabling torch.compile for this variant if needed. Keep estimate_loss, best validation loss, generation, final_info, and inference speed based on the unadapted model for direct comparability. Add validation diagnostics that report no-adaptation suffix loss, prefix-adapted suffix loss after 1 to 3 adapter-only steps, mismatched-prefix adaptation as a negative control, adaptation overhead, adapter parameter count, and generated samples after adapting on a prompt prefix. Compare the baseline, ordinary adapters without meta-training, and first-order prefix-meta adapters across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8, with small ablations over adapter rank, inner learning rate, meta loss weight, and prefix length.
